bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Strategic and demand risk — volatility in discretionary consumption — The AR flags volatility in discretionary consumption affecting dine-in traffic, pricing power and restaurant operating leverage. This was not theoretical in FY26: a subdued demand environment through the first half reduced operating leverage and, together with higher marketing, customer-acquisition and expansion spend, the Company reported a net loss of Rs 619 million even as consolidated revenue from operations rose 8.6% to Rs 13,387 million. Mitigation cited is a balanced portfolio across dine-in, premium, international and delivery formats, value and menu interventions, direct digital engagement and close monitoring of guest frequency, transactions and mix.
- Location and expansion risk on an accelerating store-opening programme — Sub-optimal site selection, format choice or ramp-up can depress restaurant returns. The Company added 35 restaurants in FY26 (14 in Q4), the highest annual expansion in recent years, taking the network to 262 as at March 31, 2026, and is targeting more than 300 restaurants in FY27 — so the risk is scaling with the pace. The AR itself notes that the opening pace and ramp-up of new Premium CDR restaurants (30 to 42 during FY26) moderated near-term margins. Mitigation: cluster-led expansion, catchment and feasibility analysis, format and capex calibration, ramp-up monitoring and post-investment performance review.
- Operational, food-safety and hygiene risk across a growing network — Operational disruption or inconsistent food and service quality across an expanding, multi-brand, multi-geography network is listed as a key business risk, alongside food-safety, hygiene or workplace-safety incidents affecting guests, employees and brand trust; the BRSR material-issues table ranks Food Safety & Quality Compliance first, as a risk with negative financial implications, on the rationale that strict regulatory requirements and customer expectations demand adherence to food safety standards. Guest-facing evidence of the exposure sits in the BRSR complaints table: 3,287 customer complaints were filed in FY2025-26 (3,004 in FY2024-25), with 21 pending resolution at the close of the year. Mitigation: standard operating procedures, restaurant and food-safety audits, monthly hygiene audits, corrective and preventive action plans, role-based and recurring training, escalation protocols, technology-enabled performance monitoring and investment in high-standard storage and preparation processes.
- Supply chain and input cost risk — Supply disruption and volatility in food, packaging, energy and logistics costs is a named risk, and the BRSR material-issues table separately identifies Climate Change & Supply Chain Disruptions as a risk with negative financial implications, on the rationale that extreme weather and climate change can disrupt food supply chains and affect costs and availability. Mitigation: diversified sourcing, strategic vendor relationships, inventory controls, procurement reviews, menu engineering, energy and cost efficiency initiatives, stronger supplier contracts and climate-resilient logistics.
- Financial risk — liquidity pressure and margin compression alongside expansion commitments — The AR names liquidity pressure, margin compression or weaker returns arising from demand volatility, input costs or expansion commitments. FY26 bore this out: consolidated EBITDA fell to Rs 2,078 million from Rs 2,272 million, and Barbeque Nation India's pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin of 10.8% was 120 basis points below the previous year. Mitigation: liquidity monitoring, capex prioritisation, restaurant-level margin reviews, cost controls and capital allocation linked to unit economics and return thresholds.
- Compliance and regulatory risk, including the new labour-code regime — Non-compliance with food safety, labour, licensing, tax and other statutes is a named risk for a business running a licensed restaurant network across many jurisdictions. A specific FY26 development was the implementation of the four Labour Codes (Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020, Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020, consolidating 29 existing labour laws) with effect from November 21, 2025, requiring the Company to realign HR policies, employment practices and compliance processes. Mitigation: defined compliance ownership, periodic reviews, audit mechanisms, licence tracking and engagement with legal and regulatory specialists.
- Consumer preference and pricing / value-proposition risk — Changes in consumer preferences, dining behaviour or cuisine relevance can reduce visit frequency, and misalignment between pricing, perceived value and customer expectations is listed as a separate risk — structurally important for an operator whose flagship is a single, distinctive live-grill casual-dining format in a market the AR describes as shifting towards QSR, delivery-led and dessert/beverage formats. Mitigation: continuous consumer insight, menu and format innovation, food festivals, portfolio diversification, market and competitor benchmarking, price-pack architecture and monitoring of traffic, mix and guest feedback.
- Emerging and geopolitical risk on the international estate — Geopolitical disruption affecting international demand, supply chains, energy costs, currency movements or business continuity is a named risk. It is material because 13 of the 262 restaurants operate across the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Malaysia, Bahrain, Sri Lanka and Saudi Arabia, and the international segment grew 28.2% to Rs 1,247 million at a pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin of 22.2% — the highest-margin part of the portfolio. Mitigation: market-level scenario planning, diversified geographic exposure, local operating oversight and agile decisions on sourcing, pricing and expansion.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: UFBL's expansion is restaurant-network build-out rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company added 35 new restaurants across formats and geographies, including 14 restaurants in the fourth quarter, taking the consolidated network to 262 restaurants as at March 31, 2026 — described as the highest annual expansion undertaken by the Company in recent years. The network comprised 249 restaurants across more than 80 Indian cities and 13 restaurants across the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Malaysia, Bahrain, Sri Lanka and Saudi Arabia. Within that, the Premium CDR portfolio (Toscano and Salt) added twelve restaurants during FY26, taking its network from 30 to 42; the opening pace and ramp-up of these new restaurants moderated near-term margins while mature restaurants continued to validate the underlying unit economics. Internationally, FY26 saw the Company establish a presence in Saudi Arabia, following entry into Sri Lanka in 2025, Bahrain in 2023, Oman in 2020, Malaysia in 2018 and the first international restaurant in Dubai, United Arab Emirates in 2016. Further international expansion is to remain focused on attractive trade areas, local operating capability and disciplined replication of the model. Expansion is cluster-led and format-conscious, guided by a cluster-based approach to site selection, catchment and feasibility analysis, format and capex calibration, rigorous evaluation of unit economics, ramp-up monitoring and post-investment performance review, with calibrated capital deployment and a sustained focus on store-level profitability. The Company states it remains on track towards more than 300 restaurants in FY27, with the quality of each addition as important as the pace of growth; the path to 300+ is to be governed by both the breadth of the platform and the quality of its economics. Portfolio expansion has also come through acquisitions that added brands and geographies — a controlling stake in Red Apple Kitchen Consultancy Private Limited (Toscano) in 2020, the acquisition of Blue Planet Foods Private Limited (Salt) in 2023, and a majority stake in Willow Gourmet Private Limited (Omm Nom Nomm) in 2025 — alongside the launch of the delivery-led brands UBQ (2018) and Dum Safar (2023). No rupee quantum of capital expenditure is stated in the narrative sections supplied.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- FY26 was shaped by a subdued discretionary demand environment in the first half that reduced operating leverage, with performance improving decisively in the second half as dine-in demand, transactions and operating leverage recovered; the year ended with a stronger demand base and a clear priority to translate growth into improved margins and returns
- Second-half recovery evidenced by gross profit up 14.3% to ₹4,860 million and restaurant operating profit up 14.6% to ₹1,044 million; Q4 FY26 delivered 14.4% SSSG and the highest-ever fourth-quarter revenue
- Improvement in SSSG, guest throughput and restaurant operating profit during the second half provides a stronger base for margin recovery in FY27
- Higher investment in marketing, customer acquisition and network expansion weighed on FY26 annual profitability
- India's foodservices market is large and underpenetrated: expected to grow from approximately US$90 billion in 2025 to over US$150 billion by 2030 (Redseer Strategy Consultants), with penetration at 13 percent of total food consumption versus 58-62 percent in the US and 42-46 percent in China
- Formalisation is a defining structural shift — organised segment growth of ~12%-14% versus ~5%-7% for the unorganised segment — as consumers gravitate to brands offering consistent quality, hygiene, food safety and digital convenience
- Dining out growth in Indian markets beyond the top eight cities is estimated at nearly two times that of the top eight cities, making Tier II and emerging cities important growth drivers
- Increasing urbanisation, rising disposable incomes, convenience-led consumption and expanding consumption occasions are lifting dining-out frequency from an occasional activity to regular social and lifestyle-driven behaviour
- Experience-led and occasion-based dining continues to gain share, benefiting celebration-led and group dining formats — the core of the Barbeque Nation proposition
- Desserts and indulgence-led categories are growing strongly on premiumisation, celebration-led consumption and strong compatibility with delivery, supporting the Omm Nom Nomm adjacency
- Digital and omnichannel adoption — online ordering, digital payments, loyalty programmes and aggregator platforms — is reshaping consumption and converging dine-in, takeaway and delivery; traditional dine-in formats are evolving towards integrated dine-in plus delivery models
- Owned-channel scale is the margin lever on customer acquisition: 60.9% of Q4 FY26 dine-in transactions through owned digital channels, 1.2 million monthly active users (up 51.2% year on year), 9.1 million cumulative app downloads and nearly 90% of dine-in transactions through captive channels including app, website, in-house call centre and walk-ins
- Delivery revenue grew 31.9% year on year in Q4 FY26 to ₹633 million from ₹480 million in Q4 FY25, lifting its share of consolidated revenue from 16.4% to 17.5%
- Competitive intensity from organised chains, regional brands, cloud kitchens and delivery-first operators may drive pricing pressure and higher customer-acquisition costs; dependence on third-party delivery ecosystems raises questions of commission structures, platform visibility and customer ownership

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: UFBL operates and manages restaurants, with food and beverages accounting for 100% of turnover. The platform is anchored by Barbeque Nation, the category creator in experiential casual dining with its fixed-price, all-you-can-eat live-grill format, and extends into premium casual dining through Toscano (Italian) and Salt (contemporary Indian), into delivery-first consumption through UBQ by Barbeque Nation, Barbeque in a Box and Dum Safar Biryani, and into premium desserts through Omm Nom Nomm. Shared capabilities in site development, procurement, operations, technology and customer engagement support growth across the portfolio, serving families, corporate teams and friends across celebrations, group occasions and everyday meals.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- FY26 was shaped by a subdued discretionary demand environment in the first half that reduced operating leverage, with performance improving decisively in the second half as dine-in demand, transactions and operating leverage recovered; the year ended with a stronger demand base and a clear priority to translate growth into improved margins and returns
- Second-half recovery evidenced by gross profit up 14.3% to ₹4,860 million and restaurant operating profit up 14.6% to ₹1,044 million; Q4 FY26 delivered 14.4% SSSG and the highest-ever fourth-quarter revenue
- Improvement in SSSG, guest throughput and restaurant operating profit during the second half provides a stronger base for margin recovery in FY27
- Higher investment in marketing, customer acquisition and network expansion weighed on FY26 annual profitability
- India's foodservices market is large and underpenetrated: expected to grow from approximately US$90 billion in 2025 to over US$150 billion by 2030 (Redseer Strategy Consultants), with penetration at 13 percent of total food consumption versus 58-62 percent in the US and 42-46 percent in China
- Formalisation is a defining structural shift — organised segment growth of ~12%-14% versus ~5%-7% for the unorganised segment — as consumers gravitate to brands offering consistent quality, hygiene, food safety and digital convenience
- Dining out growth in Indian markets beyond the top eight cities is estimated at nearly two times that of the top eight cities, making Tier II and emerging cities important growth drivers
- Increasing urbanisation, rising disposable incomes, convenience-led consumption and expanding consumption occasions are lifting dining-out frequency from an occasional activity to regular social and lifestyle-driven behaviour
- Experience-led and occasion-based dining continues to gain share, benefiting celebration-led and group dining formats — the core of the Barbeque Nation proposition
- Desserts and indulgence-led categories are growing strongly on premiumisation, celebration-led consumption and strong compatibility with delivery, supporting the Omm Nom Nomm adjacency
- Digital and omnichannel adoption — online ordering, digital payments, loyalty programmes and aggregator platforms — is reshaping consumption and converging dine-in, takeaway and delivery; traditional dine-in formats are evolving towards integrated dine-in plus delivery models
- Owned-channel scale is the margin lever on customer acquisition: 60.9% of Q4 FY26 dine-in transactions through owned digital channels, 1.2 million monthly active users (up 51.2% year on year), 9.1 million cumulative app downloads and nearly 90% of dine-in transactions through captive channels including app, website, in-house call centre and walk-ins
- Delivery revenue grew 31.9% year on year in Q4 FY26 to ₹633 million from ₹480 million in Q4 FY25, lifting its share of consolidated revenue from 16.4% to 17.5%
- Competitive intensity from organised chains, regional brands, cloud kitchens and delivery-first operators may drive pricing pressure and higher customer-acquisition costs; dependence on third-party delivery ecosystems raises questions of commission structures, platform visibility and customer ownership

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: UFBL's expansion is restaurant-network build-out rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company added 35 new restaurants across formats and geographies, including 14 restaurants in the fourth quarter, taking the consolidated network to 262 restaurants as at March 31, 2026 — described as the highest annual expansion undertaken by the Company in recent years. The network comprised 249 restaurants across more than 80 Indian cities and 13 restaurants across the United Arab Emirates, Oman, Malaysia, Bahrain, Sri Lanka and Saudi Arabia. Within that, the Premium CDR portfolio (Toscano and Salt) added twelve restaurants during FY26, taking its network from 30 to 42; the opening pace and ramp-up of these new restaurants moderated near-term margins while mature restaurants continued to validate the underlying unit economics. Internationally, FY26 saw the Company establish a presence in Saudi Arabia, following entry into Sri Lanka in 2025, Bahrain in 2023, Oman in 2020, Malaysia in 2018 and the first international restaurant in Dubai, United Arab Emirates in 2016. Further international expansion is to remain focused on attractive trade areas, local operating capability and disciplined replication of the model. Expansion is cluster-led and format-conscious, guided by a cluster-based approach to site selection, catchment and feasibility analysis, format and capex calibration, rigorous evaluation of unit economics, ramp-up monitoring and post-investment performance review, with calibrated capital deployment and a sustained focus on store-level profitability. The Company states it remains on track towards more than 300 restaurants in FY27, with the quality of each addition as important as the pace of growth; the path to 300+ is to be governed by both the breadth of the platform and the quality of its economics. Portfolio expansion has also come through acquisitions that added brands and geographies — a controlling stake in Red Apple Kitchen Consultancy Private Limited (Toscano) in 2020, the acquisition of Blue Planet Foods Private Limited (Salt) in 2023, and a majority stake in Willow Gourmet Private Limited (Omm Nom Nomm) in 2025 — alongside the launch of the delivery-led brands UBQ (2018) and Dum Safar (2023). No rupee quantum of capital expenditure is stated in the narrative sections supplied.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Category creator: pioneered the over-the-table live grill concept in India and remains one of the country's leading organised casual dining operators, giving Barbeque Nation scale and brand equity that anchors the platform
- Multi-brand portfolio designed around distinct consumer occasions, cuisines and price points, allowing participation across casual dining, premium dining, delivery and desserts
- Owned digital ecosystem: 60.9% of dine-in transactions routed through owned digital channels in Q4 FY26, 1.2 million monthly active users (up 51% year on year) and 9.1 million cumulative app downloads, reducing reliance on third-party discovery platforms
- Nearly 90% of dine-in transactions driven through captive channels including the app, website, in-house call centre and walk-ins
- Shared platform capabilities in site development, procurement, operations, technology and customer engagement that let new brands scale without replicating a full dine-in format
- Cluster-based site selection with rigorous evaluation of unit economics and focus on store-level profitability
- International format economics: pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin of 22.2% in the international segment
- Delivery-first brands leverage existing culinary expertise, kitchen infrastructure and digital capabilities to improve asset utilisation
- Data-led decision-making across demand forecasting, menu engineering, procurement and restaurant operations; AI and data intelligence used to optimise bookings and minimise cancellations

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate rename] The company is "United Foodbrands Limited (Formerly known as Barbeque-Nation Hospitality Limited)" — the listed entity has been rebranded to a multi-brand platform identity while the flagship restaurant brand remains Barbeque Nation. Scrip code BSE 543283 / NSE UFBL.
- [Shareholding] As on June 30, 2026: Promoters & Promoter Group 34.6%, Jubilant Foodworks 9.3%, institutional investors 27.8%, others 28.3% — i.e. a listed QSR peer holds a ~9% strategic stake.
- [Minority interests not adjusted] The deck's disclaimer states "All the numbers are on consolidated basis and without adjustment for the minority interest of Red Apple Kitchen Consultancy, Blue Planet Foods and Willow Gourmet unless otherwise mentioned" — consolidated figures overstate the economic interest attributable to UFBL.
- [International cost shock] International gross margins "moderated by 320 bps YoY due to inflationary pressures related to middle east crisis", and the deck's BBQ International unit economics are "based on H2 FY26, excluding temporary GCC inflationary pressures in Q1 FY27" — the segment's headline unit economics are therefore on a different, cleaner period than the other two segments.
- [Loss-making at reported level] Reported PAT was ₹(619) Mn in FY26 and ₹(270) Mn in FY25; adjusted PAT was ₹(289) Mn and ₹(31) Mn. Q1 FY27 turned to ₹23 Mn reported PAT (adjusted ₹87 Mn), so the recovery is one quarter old.
